script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. Thursday — here is your SOXX recap. The portfolio closed up ten point eight zero percent on the session. Every primary holding finished in the green. This was a broad, powerful move across the semiconductor space.

Samsung's memory earnings just changed the calculus for every memory and storage name in this portfolio. A one thousand eight hundred fourteen percent surge in operating profit, record revenue, and a forward statement that memory supply shortages will persist through twenty twenty-eight. That last point is the one that matters most right now.

The Nasdaq Composite snapped a six-day losing streak on Thursday, surging on the back of strong earnings from major technology names including Microsoft. No major macro data prints were available to complicate the picture, leaving the session largely driven by corporate earnings results and a clear rotation back into high-growth technology.

The top story Thursday belongs to Micron Technology. Samsung Electronics reported earnings that sent a direct signal to every memory investor: supply tightness is not a short-term phenomenon. Samsung posted a one thousand eight hundred fourteen percent year-over-year surge in operating profit alongside record revenue, and crucially, management indicated the memory shortage will run through twenty twenty-eight. That is a multi-year demand floor for Micron. Layered on top of that fundamental backdrop, Micron also disclosed in mid-July that it had completed multi-year strategic customer agreements with a significant roster of automotive ecosystem partners, including Qualcomm, Visteon, HARMAN, JOYNEXT, DENSO, Astemo, and Hyundai Mobis. These agreements lock in long-term access to advanced memory and storage for artificial intelligence-enabled vehicles. The combination of a tightening supply signal from the industry's largest player and a diversified automotive demand story gives Micron a layered growth thesis heading into the second half of twenty twenty-six.

Micron Technology surged eighteen point three six percent on Thursday, the largest single-session gain among the primary holdings. The Samsung earnings report and the automotive artificial intelligence supply agreements framed the move. Watch for any follow-through commentary from memory analysts revising their price targets upward in response to Samsung's supply outlook remarks.

Turning to Advanced Micro Devices, which rose thirteen point zero zero percent on the session. Multiple sources flagged server chips as a quietly overlooked growth engine, with analysts pointing out that valuation concerns on the stock dissolve significantly when modeled two years forward on an aggressive but plausible growth trajectory. The Nasdaq rebound provided additional lift. Watch for Advanced Micro Devices' upcoming earnings for confirmation of server chip revenue acceleration.

Lam Research Corporation added seventeen point nine eight percent Thursday, a standout move for a semiconductor equipment name. No single company-specific headline drove the gain, but the broader memory supply shortage narrative out of Samsung directly benefits equipment suppliers positioned for capacity expansion orders. Watch for order backlog commentary at the next earnings update.

Applied Materials rose fourteen point nine seven percent on the session. Like Lam Research, the memory shortage extension narrative is a direct demand signal for wafer fabrication equipment providers. Any indication that foundry customers are accelerating capital expenditure timelines would be the next catalyst to monitor here.

Marvell Technology gained twelve point one eight percent Thursday. No specific headline was attached to the move, but the company's exposure to data center interconnects and custom artificial intelligence silicon kept it well-correlated with the broader sector rally. Earnings guidance will be the clearest near-term indicator of momentum.

Intel Corporation climbed eleven point three zero percent on the session. No company-specific news was available Thursday. The move appears tied to the sector-wide recovery and Intel's ongoing positioning in the artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout. An update on its foundry business timeline remains the primary near-term catalyst to track.

Over at NVIDIA Corporation, the gain was two point six five percent Thursday. Investors received strong spending signals from Meta Platforms and Microsoft but tempered expectations around the pace of near-term hardware orders. One analyst source noted that NVIDIA investors were hoping for more from those earnings calls. The stock is showing signs of recovery but the relative underperformance versus sector peers Thursday is worth noting. Supply chain expansion through partners like Super Micro Computer remains a watch item.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company rose seven point six four percent on the session. As the primary contract manufacturer for nearly every chip designer in this portfolio, the Samsung supply tightness signal is a direct positive for pricing power. Any update on advanced node capacity utilization is the key forward metric.

Broadcom gained four point seven three percent Thursday, and KLA Corporation added five point nine six percent. Both moves were constructive and in line with the sector recovery, though neither led the field. Broadcom's custom artificial intelligence silicon pipeline and KLA's process control equipment demand remain the longer-term stories to follow.

Three data points to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, any analyst note revisions targeting Micron Technology following Samsung's supply outlook statement — that forward guidance could trigger a wave of estimate increases. Second, the Advanced Micro Devices earnings date confirmation, as the server chip narrative needs a revenue data point to hold. Third, any Federal Reserve speaker commentary scheduled for Friday that could shift rate expectations and pressure high-multiple technology valuations.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch closely for how the memory supply shortage narrative evolves — Samsung's remarks have set a high bar for follow-through across every name in this portfolio.
